subject: TTFT + Streaming SLOs — follow-up & next steps
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: TTFT + Streaming SLOs — post-call recap

Hi Elena – thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps on the Time-to-First-Token (TTFT) and streaming requirements you outlined: 

Summary of asks (from your team):
- TTFT target: very low latency for short responses; you mentioned sub-200ms as a target for interactive flows.
- Streaming: SSE or WebSocket support for server-sent partial tokens; should be able to tune chunk cadence – important for progressive UI.
- Throughput/concurrency: need to sustain expected peak traffic (~400 QPS) with up to ~50 concurrent user streams.
- Observability: token-level latency breakdowns and per-request traces for troubleshooting.

Proposed qualification targets (initial):
- TTFT (time to first token): 95th percentile <= 150ms, 99th <= 250ms for short-answer paths (<= 128 tokens).
- Chunk cadence (streaming): <= 200ms between chunks under normal conditions; support configurable cadence down to 100-150ms if required.
- Throughput: baseline 400 QPS with 50 concurrent streaming connections; burst to 750 QPS for short windows.
- Protocols: primary: WebSocket for bidirectional; fallback: SSE for non-bidirectional UIs.

Attachments: I’ve attached a short proposal (redwood-ttft-proposal.pdf) that outlines test methodology + sample perf matrix.

Next steps:
1) Can your engineering lead confirm the TTFT and cadence targets above, and call out any stricter 95/99 targets we should plan to test?
2) If agreed, we’ll schedule a perf validation run (week of Aug 23) with a small test harness we provide.
3) Dev will follow up with a pre-run checklist and a short-run smoke test.

Happy to hop on another 30m if helpful.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0198
From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@acmehealth.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-15T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: TTFT + Streaming SLOs 

On Mon, Aug 15, 2027 at 9:12 AM Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Hi Elena – thanks again for the call this morning...

Thanks, Aditya – this is a helpful summary. A few clarifications from our side so the perf targets match real product constraints:

- Primary TTFT expectation: for short interactive replies (<= 32 tokens), median ~80ms and 95th <= 120ms if possible. For slightly longer short replies (<= 128 tokens) 95th <= 200ms, 99th <= 300ms.
- Chunk cadence: our UX team prefers ~150ms cadence for streaming partial tokens; 200ms is acceptable as an upper bound but would slightly degrade perceived responsiveness.
- Protocols: WebSocket is our preference (we have bi-directional flows). SSE may be used for legacy clients but only as fallback.
- Throughput: the 400 QPS is accurate for peak interactive flows; we also have background batch/bulk scoring which can be routed to a different endpoint.
- Compliance note: some streams will carry PHI (HIPAA) so we'll need encryption + audit logs; we'll surface the SOC2/HIPAA questions separately with your security team.

Procurement timeline: we’re aiming to complete technical validation + security review in the next 6–8 weeks, so a perf run in the week of Aug 23 works well.

Elena Morales
Head of Product Engineering | Acme Health
elena.morales@acmehealth.com | +1 (212) 555-0102
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-15T11:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: TTFT + Streaming SLOs 

Thanks for the quick clarification, Elena – that helps a lot. Updated plan based on your notes: 

1) Targets we'll validate in perf run (week of Aug 23):
   - Short interactive (<=32 tokens): median <= 100ms target (aiming at your ~80ms), 95th <= 120ms.
   - Short (<=128 tokens): 95th <= 200ms, 99th <= 300ms.
   - Chunk cadence: default <= 150ms where feasible; fallback <= 200ms.
   - Throughput: sustain 400 QPS with 50 concurrent streams; validate burst behavior to 750 QPS.

2) Protocols: we'll validate both WebSocket and SSE; WebSocket will be primary for the perf runs.

3) Compliance & observability: I’ve looped in Marissa (Security/compliance) separately to start the SOC2/HIPAA checklist items.

4) Next operational steps:
   - Dev (Dev Patel) will share a perf-run checklist + expected data formats by EOD Tue.
   - We’ll send a short harness (script + k6 load profile) for you to run in your environment and for us to run from our infra.

Link to the short SLO doc: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1TTFT-plan (attached in proposal too).

If that all sounds good, I’ll lock in Thu Aug 26 10:00am PT as a tentative perf-run kickoff and invite engineering.

Best,
Aditya
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-15T13:45:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: Acme perf run prep (TTFT + streaming)

Internal notes / asks:
- Elena pushed for ~150ms chunk cadence and ~80ms median TTFT on very short replies. We should prioritize WebSocket path and validate SSE only as fallback.
- Prep checklist for perf run (high priority):
  * Define test harness: request mix (short <=32, short <=128, long <=512), token-per-chunk targets, and simulated user think time.
  * Measure TTFT at 50 and 95 concurrent streaming connections + 400 QPS steady state.
  * Record chunk cadence distribution (p50/p95/p99) and number of chunks per response.
  * End-to-end traces and per-token latency breakdowns exported to the shared GCS perf bucket.
  * Include a run with cold KV-cache vs warmed KV-cache to capture first-token delta.

Can you draft the initial k6 profile and a quick runbook for the Thu Aug 26 kickoff? I’ll confirm with Acme once we have the checklist.

Thanks,
Aditya
